Invalid text/day and missing leap information are named CSPICE errors. Nonzero signed/fractional epochs distinguish the old zero-only case. Separate tests cover non-string JavaScript arguments, temporary allocation failures and same-instance state/recovery; no new routines or global tolerance changes.
routines.errorAssessment: Named CSPICE errors are required for applicable invalid parsing/day/time-system/default/missing-kernel paths. TPARSE/TPICTr non-CSPICE diagnostic returns are explicitly translated and compared by meaningful diagnostic fragments. Empty strings/unsupported TOOLKIT selectors are documented typed-wrapper constraints, not claimed as equivalent CSPICE errors. Cached immutable version has no reachable successful-input error state to manufacture; its initialization allocation/error paths are separately reviewed.

routines.fixtureRationale: Only existing listed LSK data and authored epoch/string/picture inputs. Formal-calendar parsing/picture derivation do not require LSK. All external fixture bytes stay unchanged; no scientific data is generated or downloaded into tracked source.
routines.cleanup: Workflow finalizers restore pre-case CALENDAR and the nonempty SYSTEM/ZONE before common kclear/reset, on both success and failure. Kernel lifecycle unloads/clears fixture state. Direct tests retain caller defaults in finally and dispose clients. All 25 temporary allocation-failure positions, including toolkit-version initialization, verify earlier buffers released. Node serializes process state; WASM owns module state.
routines.tolerance: Existing absolute/relative 1e-12 comparison is unchanged. Complete strings and shapes compare exactly. Signed/fractional near-J2000 seconds and full UTC leap-boundary effects are distinguished. Julian outputs also carry a seconds-scale offset from the actual output, preventing large epoch scale from hiding subsecond defects; inherent double Julian-day quantization remains about 40 microseconds near J2000, not a claim of finer physical precision.

routines.semantics: The public contract exposes TOOLKIT only, rejecting other selectors. The immutable toolkit version is read through actual CSPICE; native calls its spiceVersion addon route, while WASM calls the compiled getter during initialization and caches its result per module. Caching this immutable value preserves the supported contract.

scenarios.observes: Actual version strings reach comparison before/after kernel pool changes. Direct allocation/cache tests feed two distinct module-returned versions through the getter/API and require one getter call per module; full live cases compare the real N0067 toolkit with SpiceyPy. Unsupported item is the existing contract restriction, not CSPICE diagnostic equivalence. Case: Returns toolkit version string for TOOLKIT item

The immutable toolkit version is read through actual CSPICE; native calls its spiceVersion addon route, while WASM calls the compiled getter during initialization and caches its result per module. routines.errorAssessment: Named CSPICE errors are required for applicable invalid parsing/day/time-system/default/missing-kernel paths. TPARSE/TPICTr non-CSPICE diagnostic returns are explicitly translated and compared by meaningful diagnostic fragments. Empty strings/unsupported TOOLKIT selectors are documented typed-wrapper constraints, not claimed as equivalent CSPICE errors. Cached immutable version has no reachable successful-input error state to manufacture; its initialization allocation/error paths are separately reviewed.

routines.semantics: Parses formal-calendar UTC seconds past J2000 with fixed 86400-second days and no leap-second correction or LSK requirement. Nonzero/signed/fractional dates, leap-day/second notation and day-of-year forms distinguish the old constant-zero weakness. Diagnostics are returned through errmsg by CSPICE and translated to thrown errors even when global failed remains false.

routines.semantics: Converts epochs between uniform time systems using LSK conversion constants: seconds past J2000 for ET/TDB, TAI and TT/TDT; Julian days for JED/JDTDB/JDTDT. Missing constants and bad system names are distinct named CSPICE errors. Signed/fractional input and nonzero output observe conversion rather than identity/zero substitutes.

findings.summary: The unchanged comparator permits roughly 0.2 seconds at a 2.45-million-day epoch, so raw Julian output alone weakens near-J2000 precision evidence.
findings.repair: Retain the raw epoch and additionally compare secondsPastJ2000 derived from that actual output on both sides; a 0.1-second corruption regression must fail. Tolerance is unchanged.
